desc:
For each prefix s[0..i] of the string s, find the largest integer k ≥ 1 such that the prefix can be written as some block u repeated exactly k times (u + u + ... + u, with u non-empty). Return an array of length n whose entry i is that k for the prefix of length i + 1.

Example: s = "aabaabaabaab" gives [1,2,1,1,1,2,1,1,3,1,1,4]. The prefix "aa" is "a" twice, "aabaab" is "aab" twice, "aabaabaab" is "aab" three times, and the whole string is "aab" four times. A prefix that is not a repetition counts as 1.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Checking every divisor of every prefix length against the prefix is far too slow. Use something that already knows the structure of every prefix.
A prefix of length L has smallest period L - pi[L-1]. The prefix is a perfect repetition of a block when this period divides L.
If p = L - pi[L-1] and L % p == 0, the answer for this prefix is L / p; otherwise it is 1. The smallest block gives the largest repeat count.
editorial: Let pi be the prefix function. For a string of length L, the length of the shortest period is p = L - pi[L-1] (a border of length b means the string repeats with shift L - b). The string is an exact power of a block precisely when it has a period that divides L, and in that case the smallest period p divides L too (this is the periodicity lemma for the smallest period).
So for each prefix length L: if L % p == 0 the answer is L / p, otherwise there is no proper repetition and the answer is 1. Using the smallest block yields the largest k.
One pass to build pi and one pass over the prefixes: O(n) time, O(n) space.
